title: Millionaire's Shortbread
summary: Three-layer tray bake with a buttery shortbread base, a thick cooked caramel middle, and a firm chocolate topping, cut into neat squares.
equipment: 20 cm square metal baking tin (not glass), lined with a baking-paper sling
sharp knife and jug of hot water

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt, or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt, or table salt

steps.title: Heat oven, line tin
steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) for at least 20 minutes before baking. Line the 20cm metal tin with a baking-paper sling to make lifting out the finished bars straightforward later.

steps.title: Make the shortbread base
steps.text: Pulse or rub the flour, cornflour, sugar, salt and cold cubed butter together until the mixture clumps into coarse crumbs. Press it firmly and evenly into the tin, then prick all over with a fork — docking lets steam escape so the base doesn't bubble up unevenly.

steps.title: Bake the base
steps.text: Bake for 25-30 minutes, until pale golden and firm at the edges, then leave to cool in the tin. A firm, fully cooled base keeps the shortbread crisp once the wet caramel goes on top.

steps.title: Cook the caramel
steps.text: In a heavy-based pan over medium-low heat, melt the condensed milk, butter, brown sugar, golden syrup and salt together, stirring. Keep cooking, stirring constantly and scraping the base so the sugars can't catch, for 8-12 minutes until thick, a shade darker and 113-115°C — it should leave a clear trail when you draw the spatula through it.

steps.title: Pour and cool the caramel
steps.text: Pour the hot caramel over the cooled base and level it off, then leave to cool for 15 minutes before chilling for 1 hour until firm. Chilling sets the caramel enough to take the weight of the chocolate layer without the two mixing together.

steps.title: Add the chocolate topping
steps.text: Melt the chocolate and butter gently in a bowl over simmering water until smooth, then spread over the firm caramel. Chill for 30 minutes until set — the butter keeps the chocolate from setting too hard to cut cleanly.

steps.title: Cut into squares
steps.text: Leave at room temperature for 10 minutes, then cut into 16 squares using a knife dipped in hot water and wiped dry between cuts, for slices through the chocolate without cracking it.

tips: Stir the caramel constantly and scrape the base of the pan — sugar that catches on the bottom will scorch and turn the whole batch bitter.
Use a thermometer if you have one; caramel cooked only to 113-115°C sets with a proper chew, while an underdone caramel stays runny once cut.
Chill the caramel layer fully before adding the chocolate, or the two layers will merge instead of staying distinct.
Dip the knife in hot water and dry it before each cut for clean squares without cracked or smeared chocolate.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 1 week, or freeze for up to 2 months. Let come to room temperature for about 15 minutes before serving so the caramel softens.
